author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새 수만 마리 · 여름철새 수십 마리 · 겨울에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
habitat: 해안 모래밭, 갯벌, 강 하구, 물 고인 논, 하천가
summary: 봄과 가을에 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새이다. 해안의 모래밭, 갯벌, 강 하구, 물이 고인 논, 하천가에서 대개 큰 무리를 이루어 지내며 갑각류, 갯지렁이, 물속 곤충 등 여러 무척추동물을 잡아먹는다. 유라시아 대륙 북부와 알래스카 서부에서 번식하고 유럽, 아프리카, 중동, 동남아시아, 호주에서 겨울을 난다.

points.en: long upturned dark bill with pink base
breeding male: rufous from head to belly
non-breeding: grey-brown upperparts marked dark brown

sexes.male: 여름깃은 머리에서 배까지 적갈색이고 몸 윗면은 적갈색 반점이 있는 흑갈색이다.
sexes.female: 수컷보다 크고 부리도 길며, 여름깃의 적갈색이 연하고 몸 윗면이 어둡게 보인다.

art.subject: Bar-tailed Godwit (Limosa lapponica), adult male in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean tidal flats during spring migration (April–May): head, neck and entire underparts to the belly deep rufous-chestnut, the crown finely streaked dark; mantle and scapulars blackish-brown with rufous notches and fringes; wing coverts greyer brown. Bill very long, slightly upturned, mostly dark with a pinkish base. Dark eye. Long blackish legs.
art.pose: probing the mud with its long bill on a tidal flat
art.scene: Korean tidal mudflat at a river mouth with a large flock of shorebirds; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male breeding, side view standing: very long gently upturned bill with pink base and dark tip, deep rufous-chestnut head, neck and underparts to the belly, blackish-brown upperparts spotted rufous, long dark legs
adult female breeding, side view standing: larger body and noticeably longer bill, underparts only washed pale rufous-buff or largely whitish, upperparts duller and greyer with dark feather centres

adult non-breeding, side view standing: grey-brown upperparts with dark brown shaft streaks, pale supercilium, finely streaked grey breast, greyish-white underparts, long dark legs, pink-based upturned bill
art.build: Large, long-billed, long-legged wader, 38.5–41cm, about the length of a feral pigeon but much longer-legged and with a far longer bill; females distinctly larger and longer-billed than males. Bill very long (around twice the head length, longest in females), slender, with a gentle upturn mainly along its outer half; pinkish base, dark distal half. Legs long and blackish with bare tibia showing, though shorter than in Black-tailed Godwit. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip or slightly beyond. Tail short and closely barred. In flight no white wing-bar; rump and tail barred, with no black tail band.
avoid: Do not paint a straight bill, a broad white wing-bar or a black tail band — those belong to Black-tailed Godwit (Limosa limosa).
Do not paint a downcurved bill (curlews and Whimbrel).
Do not curve the bill strongly like an avocet; the upturn is gentle and mostly in the outer half.
Do not give breeding females the deep chestnut of males; females are much paler below.
